title: orbitopt Earth->Mars transfer mission config v1.0
description: A user-editable YAML/JSON config for the Earth-launch-to-Mars-orbit-insertion mission (orbitopt.viz.mars_transfer.build_from_config), letting a user tune the departure window, parking orbit, time-of-flight search range, target Mars capture orbit, and the optimizer/propagation knobs without touching source. Same strictness convention as mission-geo-raising-1.0.json (additionalProperties: false everywhere) -- catching a typo'd field name here, before any compute runs, is the entire point of `orbitopt validate`. Every section besides `mission` and `output` is optional; an omitted section (or omitted leaf field within a present section) falls back to orbitopt's own built-in defaults -- the same values the 'mars' built-in mission already uses. This mission ends at Mars orbit insertion, not a landing -- this framework has no atmosphere model (see orbitopt.viz.mars_transfer's module docstring).

schemaVersion.description: Which version of this mission-config schema the document was written against.

id.description: Stable slug for the produced scene, e.g. 'mars-transfer'.

launch_window.description: The Earth departure date range the porkchop screen + optimizer search over. Defaults to a real near-term Earth-Mars Hohmann-class window (2026-09 through 2027-02) if omitted.

parking_orbit.description: The Earth parking orbit the trail starts from before the TMI burn. Defaults to a 185 km circular parking orbit (matches the Artemis II mission's convention) if omitted.

launch.description: Optional real launch: site, rocket, payload and parking orbit (orbitopt.launch_injection). When present (and enabled), the (t0, tof) search applies the vehicle C3 / site DLA launch constraints, and the flown trajectory starts from a launch-window lift-off into a site-reachable parking orbit with a numerically verified TMI burn (verification report kind 'launch-injection'). Omit it (or set enabled: false) for the original behaviour: an idealized parking orbit with no site or rocket.

site.description: Launch-site id / name / alias from orbitopt's launch-site database, e.g. 'ksc'.

vehicle.description: Launch-vehicle key from orbitopt's launch-vehicle database, e.g. 'atlas-v-551'. Omit to check only the site DLA limit.

payload_kg.description: Injected mass; sets the vehicle's C3 capability.

constraint_mode.description: How the search treats C3/DLA violations (orbitopt.launch_constraints).

parking_orbit.description: Parking orbit the vehicle inserts into. altitude_km defaults to the top-level parking_orbit.altitude_km (else 185 km).

min_coast_s.description: Minimum parking-orbit coast before the TMI burn. Default 600 s.

ascent_time_s.description: Lift-off to parking-orbit insertion. Default 600 s.

ascent_downrange_deg.description: Downrange arc of the kinematic ascent. Default 20 deg.

window.description: Daily launch-window selection on the departure day.

days.description: Span searched from 00:00 UTC of the departure day. Default 1.

preferred_liftoff_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant; the window whose optimum is nearest it is flown (default: the first window).

departure.description: Pin the Earth->Mars transfer instead of searching for it (e.g. to replay a flown mission's real departure).

utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC departure epoch (a bare date means 00:00 UTC).

tof_search.description: Time-of-flight bounds (days) the optimizer searches within. Defaults to 130-320 days if omitted.

mars_arrival_orbit.description: The target captured orbit at Mars. periapsis_km also doubles as the trajectory-correction maneuver's aim point. Defaults to a ~500 km periapsis altitude x 20,000 km apoapsis altitude captured ellipse if omitted.

periapsis_km.description: Target periapsis radius from Mars center (not altitude).

campaign_search.description: How the optimizer searches (t0, tof) for the minimum-dv Lambert transfer within the launch window and time-of-flight bounds.

scene_file.description: Where `orbitopt run` writes the produced scene-1.0.json document; overridable with --out.

verification_report.description: Where `orbitopt run` writes the machine-readable verification report (verification-report-1.0.json schema). Default: next to the scene as <scene stem>.verification.json.
